subject: physical-education
essentialQuestion: How does each way of travelling work, and when is each one useful?

prompts.prompt: Name the movement cues for walking and running form and explain what each one does.
Show, describe, or diagram hopping, jumping, and safe landings. A demonstration, a spoken description, and a drawing are equally valid.
Apply skipping, galloping, and sliding in a new movement task at a challenge level you select. Control and cue use are assessed, not speed, distance, or count.
A made-up learner is struggling with leaping and chasing, fleeing, dodging. Identify the likely cue or decision at fault, correct it, and explain why the correction helps.
Connect walking and running form with combining locomotor patterns. Explain how one supports the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Build and perform a short travel sequence that uses at least four different locomotor patterns and two pathways, and explain the cue you relied on most.
Describe one way you adapted a task so it worked for you, and one activity from this unit you would choose to do again. There is no wrong answer here.
